html:
SMTO-TSK-0042 — The waiting tasks changed before your change was applied

GUID: 6a74e479-d81b-4d55-a6a7-401b1b34dc77
Slug: task-queue-revision-conflict
Domain: TSK · Subsystem: tsk

What happened

  • The list of waiting tasks changed, perhaps because a task started, finished or was edited elsewhere. SMTO didn't apply your change so it wouldn't act on the wrong task.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Wait a moment for the Queued list to refresh, or reload the page. Your change was based on an older version of the list.
  2. Check the current order, and whether the task you meant is still waiting, already running, or no longer blocked. The task may already have started or moved on its own.
  3. Make your change again on the refreshed list, for example with ↑ or ↓, Start task, Skip or Run next. A change made on the current list is applied straight away.

What success looks like

  • The Queued list shows the order you wanted, or the task you chose starts.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't press the queue buttons repeatedly while the list is still changing; wait for it to settle.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A queue control (reorder, Start task on a blocked item, Skip or advance a stalled request, Run next after a failure) carried an outdated lane version, next-task identity or dependency state.

What this means

  • A queue edit/control uses an outdated lane version, next-task identity or blocked-dependency state. Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.

Why this can happen

  • A queue edit/control uses an outdated lane version, next-task identity or blocked-dependency state.

How to diagnose it

  • Refresh lane version, current ordering and dependency status; the code does not prove another client caused the change.

How to fix it

  • Re-read the lane (version, queued_tasks order, dependency state, run_next_available) and resend the control with the current version and next-task ID. The rejection does not prove another client made the change.
  • Refresh the queue and review its current version, order and dependency state before applying the intended edit.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The reviewed action matches the current version and intended next eligible task.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
